verdict.summary: Issue #215 is blocked: its claimed inherited scope is not fully preserved, the active delivery lane is unverifiable, boundaries with related work are undefined, and acceptance and rollout are not objectively specified.

blockingFindings.title: Claimed unchanged scope omits required publication invariants
blockingFindings.details: In marius-patrik/Andromeda issue #215 at version 5b5b6a8cdd4638abc6ace3043b340ec4ac70d068be1ec867be2bf5ed4de2ea4b, the body says closed issue #149 is carried unchanged, but it omits #149's explicit Windows-only transient-error allowlist, EEXIST exclusive-publication loser behavior, abandoned-temp cleanup, complete-content visibility, immutable manifest identity, and repeated contention coverage. The contract must incorporate those invariants explicitly or identify owner-approved scope changes; an implementation cannot safely infer them through an untrusted reference.

blockingFindings.title: No single verified execution and integration lane is established
blockingFindings.details: The recorded DarkFactory worker lane is blocked, while an owner-associated comment only claims that PR #240 and commit 6a8388af48486d2d48041ae7f94adda2b4ea1a5e are ready. The supplied trusted state does not verify that PR's current head, target branch, checks, merge state, ancestry, or correspondence to the current issue version. Issue #215 remains open with df:blocked. The contract must select one lane and record its verified dependency and handoff state before execution or closure.

blockingFindings.title: Scope boundaries and related-work ownership are ambiguous
blockingFindings.details: The phrase "all state publication paths" does not enumerate the projections, backups, and manifest publishers in scope or define non-goals. It also does not distinguish publication retry behavior from open issue #243's Windows state-lock lifecycle work. The issue must name the owned paths and explicitly assign or exclude overlapping lock, scheduler, handle-delay, and recovery behavior so two lanes cannot modify the same invariant independently.

blockingFindings.title: Acceptance, validation coverage, and rollout are not objectively bounded
blockingFindings.details: Acceptance says operations eventually publish or fail loudly, but specifies no retry ceiling, backoff bounds, retryable error set, terminal-error assertions, cleanup assertions, contention cases, or observable definition of prior-state preservation. It references closed issue #206 R3 without stating the required Windows and POSIX test matrix for this change, and provides no merge, release, monitoring, rollback, or issue-closure evidence requirements. These criteria must be made measurable while leaving command execution evidence to the independent exact-head Validate gate.

verdict.summary: Issue #215 is blocked by unresolved integration authority, a missing owner-escalation label, and acceptance coverage that does not objectively prove several required publication invariants.

blockingFindings.title: The sole integration lane remains unauthorized
blockingFindings.details: For marius-patrik/Andromeda issue #215 at verified version 530d4de84554554c7ace3604076dc27c58ff5a67cc05812d365e8fd4cbb40114, trusted state establishes only the open issue version and repository default branch. It does not establish an authenticated owner decision for PR #240 or a verified base, exact head, anchor inclusion, scope correspondence, merge state, integration commit, ancestry, or exact-head checks. The expected state is one explicitly owner-authorized integration lane backed by trusted live verification. Obtain the stated owner decision and verify every listed fact before execution or closure; until then the result is blocked.

blockingFindings.title: The required owner-escalation label is absent
blockingFindings.details: The verified target data lists P1, df:blocked, and df:class:hard, while the current contract and trusted label policy require df:ask-owner for the unresolved decision. Add df:ask-owner through the trusted control plane while retaining df:blocked. Without it, the durable GitHub state does not expose the required owner escalation.

blockingFindings.title: Acceptance does not prove atomic read visibility or retry identity stability
blockingFindings.details: The contract requires overwrite readers to observe only complete old or new content with no absence, and requires retries to reuse one complete payload and immutable manifest identity. The acceptance cases check final publication, preservation after failure, and exclusive-writer contention, but do not explicitly require concurrent-reader observation throughout overwrite replacement or compare payload and identity across injected retry attempts. Add objective repeated coverage for every applicable overwrite publisher that observes the destination during replacement and asserts no ENOENT or partial content, plus assertions that payload digest and manifest identity remain unchanged across every retry. Otherwise an implementation can satisfy the stated tests while violating required invariants.

blockingFindings.title: Failure-injection coverage does not enforce the retry allowlist boundary
blockingFindings.details: The invariants define operation-specific handling for EPERM, EACCES, EBUSY, and conditional exclusive-link ENOENT, but acceptance requires only one retryable failure and one representative non-retryable error. That does not prove that every allowed combination retries or that ENOENT without the stated written-fsynced-closed prerequisite, listed codes from unrelated operations, and all unlisted errors fail on their first occurrence. Require table-driven positive and negative injection coverage for the complete allowlist boundary on each applicable publisher category.
